summary: Linn Fire Patrol lookout built in 1953 on a 10-foot enclosed base; removed or destroyed in the 1970s; no source describes the site now.

facts.design: 10-foot enclosed base with an L-4 cab on top; the lookout house is given as 14 x 14 feet
facts.status_note: Removed or destroyed in the 1970s; the register and firelookout.com differ on how
facts.agency: Linn Fire Patrol (listed as Linn FPA)

events.note: Built in 1953 per the register and firelookout.com; a March 6, 1953 Albany Democrat-Herald item had announced the new station
Sources give only the 1970s; the register says removed, firelookout.com says destroyed

evidence.supports: built in 1953; 10-foot enclosed base with an L-4 cab; removed in the 1970s
evidence.quote: Built in 1953, this 10' enclosed base with an L-4 cab on top was removed in the 1970s.

evidence.supports: newspaper item on a new lookout station south of Mill City in the Tom Rock area
evidence.quote: a new lookout station in the Tom Rock area south of Mill City

evidence.supports: item dated March 6, 1953 (the March 1953 item the story cites) announcing the new station; the Albany newspaper item
evidence.quote: Among the improvements planned by the association this year is a new lookout station in the Tom Rock area south of Mill City.

evidence.supports: the item is from the Albany Democrat-Herald
station would protect the Thomas Creek basin
evidence.quote: The lookout will provide more protection for the Thomas Creek basin.

evidence.supports: patrol's count would rise to eleven lookouts
evidence.quote: It will bring to 11 the number of lookouts under Linn Fire Patrol jurisdiction

evidence.supports: 14 x 14 lookout house on a 10-foot enclosed tower
evidence.quote: 1953: A 14 x 14 lookout house constructed on a 10-foot enclosed tower.
Built in 1953, this 10' enclosed base with an L-4 cab on top was destroyed in the 1970's.

corrections.why: 3.0 m is the height of the 10-foot enclosed base only; no source gives a total height that includes the L-4 cab

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com gives the lookout's life as 1952 to the 1970s; the register and the 1953 newspaper item point to 1953
The register says removed in the 1970s; firelookout.com says destroyed in the 1970s

notes_for_editor: The register lists a Date Registered of May 14, 2011, and Administered by Linn FPA (both visible in the cached firetower.org text). No registration event is added because the story covers the lookout's history, not the listing. No staffing, fire or access information was found in the sources read. The brief's height_m of 3.0 m is the base only (see corrections). The story names the agency as the Linn Fire Patrol, the name used in the 1953 newspaper item; the register and firelookout.com abbreviate it as Linn FPA.
